titleStmt.title: Kephalaia of the Teacher, edition page 103: diplomatic and Leiden transcription

sourceDesc.bibl: Kephalaia (Manichäische Handschriften der Staatlichen Museen Berlin), ed. H. J. Polotsky and A. Böhlig, Stuttgart: Kohlhammer, 103. Restorations, sublinear dots, gap counts and corrections are the editors'.

encodingDesc.p: EpiDoc. Read by eye from the page image; gap counts, sublinear dots and supralinear stroke extents verified by measurement on the image. A supralinear stroke is marked on every letter it covers by at least half its width. Spaces are the edition's word division. Facsimile zones are measured line centres. The editors' German statements are not transcribed: each is mapped to an id of the controlled vocabulary data/kephalaia/editorial_vocabulary.json and carried as @ana (ed: statements in the text, app: apparatus footnotes, tr: categories of the transcriber's commentary).

div.p: The manuscript page number ⲣⲅ (top right, odd page) with a bar above and below as the frame (no strokes). Running title > · ⲙⲡⲥⲁϩ · < with its ornaments, no stroke. The text column starts at 481 on this page. Every dot run was counted from the dot x-positions. Every ϣ on the page was checked at 4.5–8× (one sheet): only the first ϣ of 24 ⲛⲁⲧϣϣⲓ has a dot in the lower bowl; all have their tail. ⲯ in ⲯⲓⲥ (l. 9), ⲧⲉϥⲯⲩⲭⲏ (l. 14) and ⲧⲑⲗⲓⲯⲓⲥ (l. 16): arms curving upwards and a stem through the baseline (7–8×), against the straight ϯ of ⲡϯⲟⲩ (l. 1) and ⲛϥϯ (l. 18). Kephalaion 39 (opened 102.13) runs through the whole page. Reconcile flags explained: l. 6 the foot of ⲗ of ⲛⲁϭⲱⲗⲡ (985/520); l. 11 the dot under ϭ (697) has area 5; l. 12 the third bracket dot (545) is below the ink threshold; l. 13 the eight bracket dots stand at the zone centre (y 809); l. 14 counts a break in ⲏ of ⲛⲧⲉϥⲯⲩⲭⲏ (879); l. 33 the colon (787).
